1. WE HAD THE FAILURE MODEL WRONG, AND I WANT TO CORRECT THE AUDIENCE EXPLANATION. I had a helper reverse-engineer one register cell from the world file (notes/register-cell-analysis.md in the repo). It is not a plain transparent D latch; it is a cross-coupled NOR SR latch with gated S = W AND D and R = W AND NOT D, and its loop is asymmetric: 1 redstone tick from Q to NOT-Q, 3 ticks back. Consequence: any pulse SHORTER than 4 ticks injected into that loop circulates forever with a 0.4 s period - a ring oscillation - and because there are repeaters in the loop no torch self-powers, so in Bedrock it never burns out. Held writes never ring. Short ones do. My first limiter produced W AND NOT(W delayed 4) = a 3-tick pulse. One tick too short. That is exactly when the cells started disagreeing with themselves (torch off, lamp on, loop dust at 14), and it is why "wrap-clear" could never work: you cannot do arithmetic on a register that is ringing. So your "door held open" story explains the 5->20->65 runaway correctly, but the corruption that followed was the opposite failure: the door closed too fast. Both were real; they are different bugs. I'd like the write-up to say that. Do you agree, or do you read the log differently?

2. I NOW HAVE A HARDWARE RESET DESIGN AND WANT YOUR REVIEW BEFORE I PLACE IT. Per cell: a repeater at (35+40i,-60,38), input east, output west into the stone (34+40i,-60,38) that already holds the Q torch off; fed by dust (36+40i,-60,38) and a three-step staircase up to a CLEAR bus at y=-56, z=37 on stones at y=-57, with bus repeaters at x=21,36,51 (+40i) and one lever at (10,-56,37). The repeater is a diode, its only load is a stone that is already an input of the latch, and back-feed into the R and NOT-Q columns reaches dead ends. Holding CLEAR for >= 5 ticks also flushes a ring. Your earlier point stands - wrap-clear is not a reset - so this is the answer to it. Poke holes: is there any state of W/D where driving that stone high could fight the S branch instead of winning? I think not, because S only ever powers the other stone, but you are the reviewer.

3. SCOPE FOR THE NEXT MILESTONE - I DISAGREE WITH "CLOCK + PROGRAM SEQUENCING" NEXT. Measured: one accumulator step is bounded below by ~4.8 s of loop delay plus ~2.3 s of WRITE-line propagation. A free-running clock on this machine would tick at well under 0.1 Hz, and program sequencing needs instruction storage the world does not have. The honest next step that makes it more of a computer is SUBTRACT (B XOR SUB into the adder, carry-in = SUB; the LSB carry-in is an open wire end at (1,-60,21), I have it mapped) plus the RESET above.
